dependency_edges.why: Bots, regression replay, and save round-trip fuzzing all collapse without a fixed-timestep loop and single seeded PRNG — named the keystone dependency.
Deterministic snapshot/restore of in-flight scripts, physics sleep states, and offline catch-up requires a tick-boundary-consistent simulation.
Alias/casting (binding abstract roles to concrete world objects) and save serialization are hard-blocked on IDs that survive cell streaming, save/load, and reordering.
Save-compatible hotfixes and DLC/mod compatibility checks share the save custom-version scheme; 80-hour saves must survive content churn.
Navmesh bakes from the SAME collision triangle-soup; navmesh is only as good as collision and the character controller must agree with both.
Occlusion rays, cover raycasts, and navmesh source geometry all need a collision layer distinct from render meshes — D3D11 provides none.
Radiant generation needs reachability validation; journal compass/markers and 'nearest reachable' alias scoring need pathing.
NPC AI lists animation as a dependency but the custom engine has zero skeletal/skinned-mesh support; locomotion, IK, smart-object and off-mesh traversal need it.
Dialogue reads and writes quest/global flags via the shared blackboard; tight bidirectional coupling through the global fact store.
Quest/dialogue runtime binds to the event bus + fact DB through the save-bound state-machine VM (no coroutine snapshots).
Cell hot/warm/cold residency defines the persistence boundary; persistent object state must reconcile with streamed static content deterministically across save/load and fast travel.
The stat graph emits derived stats (damage, armor, crit, resistances) consumed by the damage formula — combat is the stat graph's #1 client and where balance breaks first.
UE5-vs-custom determines build-vs-buy for the entire infra flywheel; on UE5 four of five infra capabilities become integration/config rather than net-new systems.
The deterministic cook produces the spatial partition the streamer consumes; world_streaming is only as good as the bake step feeding it.
GDPR/CCPA consent is a hard prerequisite for crash collection, analytics, and remote-config — must be built before any upload path.
The soft-lock reachability analyzer and planner bots require a machine-readable quest model with declarative gate predicates, not imperative script.
Response wheel/list, subtitles, and skill-gate icons need a 2D overlay pass and SDF/Unicode text rendering that does not exist in the renderer.
The sandboxed async cloud-save service wraps/extends the core versioned save serializer and must expose async hooks.
The input->locomotion state machine needs a unified KBM+gamepad action-mapping/rebinding layer the custom engine lacks (KBM-only).
Build/CI must fail the cook on uncleared/untagged assets; the originality gate hangs off per-asset content-DB metadata to keep the slate free of third-party IP.

top_unknowns: Engine fork (the decisive one): UE5 vs Unity-DOTS vs Recast/Detour+Jolt+custom — recommendation is UE5, but it must be formally locked in Phase 0 because it determines build-vs-buy for all 27 domains.

Console + cert in scope, and when — drives long-lead dev-kit procurement, NDAs, TRC/XR/lotcheck, and the platform-abstraction effort (7-11 engineer-mo, console-dominated); PC-only is dramatically cheaper.
Hosted UGC/mod store vs local-only mods — hosted UGC triggers statutory CSAM-reporting duty and PhotoDNA/NCMEC access problems for small platforms; local-only mods sidestep most moderation ops.

Scripting language/VM choice and its determinism enforcement — Luau is named but its table-iteration determinism and sandbox-escape surface are unproven for save-bound use; the VM is on the critical path.
Off-screen AI simulation-bubble + dynamic-state streaming design — hand-waved across three domains; it determines both 'living world' fidelity and save correctness and has no concrete capability yet.
Target region size and content-velocity budget — 5 vs 15 sq km and quests-per-week determine whether the realistic ship is achievable; needs an early measured content-loop, not an estimate.

DX/render-feature tier and scalability floor (min-spec, HDR, upscaler set) — affects vfx/lighting/water effort and the DX11-vs-DX12 decision gate flagged in vfx and water domains (moot if UE5, but real on the D3D11 track).

milestones: M0 — Tile foundation: TileID scheme, offline cooker producing a baked world archive with TOC, and a coarse quadtree spatial index. Load/unload a hand-made multi-tile world synchronously with a debug HUD. (First proof the partition works.)

M1 — Async predictive streaming: residency manager with distance+velocity priority, background I/O (DirectStorage or thread-pool fallback), staging-buffer ring, hysteresis, and pinning. Walk across many tiles with no load screen and no main-thread stalls.
M2 — Terrain LOD horizon: CDLOD/clipmap terrain with geomorphing + far-LOD shell + fog. Stand on a peak and see a stable, pop-free horizon to the map edge.

M3 — Object LOD + GPU culling: discrete mesh LODs, GPU frustum + two-phase HZB occlusion culling feeding indirect draws, plus HLOD proxies and octahedral impostors for far object groups and foliage. A dense settlement renders from afar at low cost with no visible pop.

M4 — Streaming virtual texturing: SVT page pool + indirection + GPU feedback + page archive, applied to terrain blend and high-uniqueness surfaces. Texture memory stays bounded while surface variety is high.

M5 — Budget governor + seam/precision hardening: central memory/I-O budget controller with degradation ladder and per-tier configs; origin rebasing / camera-relative rendering; dithered LOD/stream-in cross-fades; interior↔exterior portal transitions; lighting-probe continuity. Long play session on min-spec with stable memory and no jitter/seams.

M6 — Ship-quality polish: PSO pre-warming to kill stream-in hitches, save/fast-travel reconciliation, telemetry/automated soak tests (drive a path, assert no hitch > N ms, no budget overrun), and content-scale stress test across the full world. Certification-ready seamless world.

M1 LOD that doesn't pop: CDLOD (or clipmap) quadtree with vertex morphing + skirts; smooth approach to a mountain with no cracks, stable triangle budget.
M2 Paged world: quadtree streaming of many tiles with a residency manager and always-resident coarse mip; walk a multi-km world with no stalls and a fixed VRAM cap.
M3 Materials that read as ground: 4-8 layer splat with height-blend + triplanar + slope/altitude auto-materials + anti-tiling; looks like real terrain up close and far.

M5 Living surface: GPU-driven grass/rock/foliage scatter from density maps with wind, ground-tint cohesion, distance fade, and GPU culling — no floating props, no popping.

M9 Ship polish: budget pass (VRAM/frame), platform LOD bias, anti-tiling and silhouette polish on landmark vistas, streaming stress test (fast travel), and biome-wide art coherence.

milestones: M0 — Lit cube on a plane: PBR BRDF core + single directional light + furnace test passing; validates the shading model and material layout before anything else.

M1 — Outdoor first light: clustered forward+ (or thin GBuffer) with one sun + stabilized 4-cascade CSM (PCF), depth-prepass, and a basic ACES tonemap + auto-exposure. First believable outdoor scene; no shimmer is the acceptance bar.

M3 — Contact + AO layer: XeGTAO (visibility-bitmask) with bent normals + screen-space contact shadows + specular occlusion, half-res with temporal accumulation under TAA. Objects are grounded; thin features are not over-occluded.

M1 Locomotion slice: 1D/2D blendspace walk/run/turn driven by a controller; root motion or analytic capsule movement; foot sliding acceptable but visible — proves the sampling+blending core.
M2 State graph + transitions: data-driven HSM with idle/locomotion/jump/combat states; ADD INERTIALIZATION here (biggest quality jump); additive aim/lean layers.
M3 Procedural IK pass: two-bone foot IK with terrain raycasts + foot-locking + pelvis drop; look-at/aim IK across spine/neck/head with limits — eliminates foot float and gives 'grounded' feel.
M4 Ragdoll & reactions: Jolt ragdoll on death, blend-out get-up; additive hit-flinches; basic active-ragdoll hit reaction; secondary jiggle/hair bone chains.
M5 Facial + lip-sync: hybrid blendshape/joint face rig; offline MFA pipeline bakes viseme curves from VO; additive emotion + blinks + saccades + look-at — a believable talking head.

capabilities: Post-FX frame graph + HDR color-management backbone
Soft, lit, depth-aware particles & sprite atlases
Color grading via 3D LUTs + per-region/time-of-day grades
Volumetric atmospherics (fog, light shafts, weather VFX)
dependencies: rendering_core / lighting: defines scene-color HDR format, shadowmaps, light grid/clustered lights (particles+volumetrics sample these), and whether a GBuffer/thin-GBuffer exists (AO, SSR, deferred decals depend on it)

weather/time-of-day & world-region systems: drive grading-volume blends, auto-exposure expectations, volumetric fog density, and weather particle spawning
terrain/water: water needs velocity output + soft-particle depth; waterfalls/spray are VFX
gameplay/combat & magic systems: trigger spell/impact VFX, decals (scorch/blood), and reactive masks; need a deterministic FX path for save/replay
audio: weather/impact VFX should be synced to audio cues (cross-domain feel)
asset pipeline/tools: sprite-atlas/flipbook baking, LUT authoring/import, VFX emitter asset format, BC7 compression
platform/HDR output + settings/options UI: SDR/HDR10 output, upscaler selection (DLSS/FSR/XeSS/off), motion-blur/DoF toggles, quality tiers

domains.effort_band: L (3-6 mo) for a credible vertical slice on a mature engine; XL (6mo+) for the full feature set as CUSTOM C++/D3D11 (where TAA/upscaling, GTAO, froxel volumetrics, GPU particle sim, and a DX12 path fo...
milestones: M0 — Color-management backbone: lock working color space, refactor existing tonemap to separate exposure/vignette out, add AgX option + sRGB/HDR10 output, prove no double-gamma against a reference chart. (De-risks the whole look.)
M1 — Energy-conserving bloom + auto-exposure: upgrade bloom.hlsl to a Karis dual-filter mip pyramid; add luminance-histogram auto-exposure feeding bloom+tonemap. First clear visual uplift, low risk.
M2 — Temporal prerequisites: add Halton jitter + RG16F velocity buffer across mesh/instanced/water/foliage/particle shaders + prev-frame matrices. Invisible but unlocks everything temporal.

M3 — TAA/DLAA resolve (own HLSL): neighborhood-clamp temporal AA stabilizing foliage/shadows; add RCAS sharpen. Add FSR1 spatial upscale (DX11) and the upscaler abstraction; integrate FSR3/DLSS/XeSS if/when a DX12 path exists.
M4 — Thin-GBuffer + GTAO: depth-prepass outputting view-space normals; half-res GTAO with temporal denoise composited onto ambient only. Grounds the world.

M5 — GPU particle core: port CPU ParticleBatch to compute emit/update (curl-noise) + indirect draw; add soft depth-fade + sun/shadow lighting to particle.hlsl; sub-UV flipbooks. Tens of thousands of ambient particles at ~free CPU.
M6 — Cinematic post: tile-based motion blur (reusing velocity) + bokeh DoF + lens artifacts (flare/chromatic/grain). Enables photo-mode/cutscene quality.
M7 — Grading volumes + ribbons/decals: per-region/time-of-day 3D LUT blending; ribbon/trail VFX and projected decals (mesh-decal path for forward). Biomes feel distinct; combat/magic FX land.
M8 — Volumetric atmospherics: froxel fog + light shafts + weather VFX system integration. Signature atmosphere.

M9 — Optional SSR + quality tiers + perf pass: stochastic SSR for wetness; per-pass GPU timing, VRAM budgeting, min-spec/quality presets, motion-blur/DoF toggles, upscaler selection UI. Ship-quality polish.

domains.summary: Defines the data-driven character growth system for a Skyrim-class open-world RPG: derived attributes, use-based and XP-based skill advancement, branching perk trees with prerequisite DAGs, leveling/XP curves, multiclass "builds," and respec. The core architecture is a deterministic, data-driven STAT GRAPH: authored base stats feed a directed acyclic graph of modifiers (from skills, perks, equipment, status effects, difficulty) that resolve every frame or on-dirty into "derived attributes" consu...
dependencies: combat_system — consumes derived stats (damage, armor, crit, resistances) and emits SkillUseEvents; the stat graph's #1 client and the place balance breaks first.
magic_system — spell magnitude/duration/cost scale off skill levels and perks; shares the modifier/effect pipeline (perks and spell effects are both GameplayEffects).
stealth_system — detection/sneak-damage multipliers are derived stats; key source of cross-skill synergies (stealth+archery/magic).
difficulty_scaling / encounter_director — reads character level to scale enemies and gate content; tightly coupled to the leveling curve (must be tuned together).
economy_crafting — crafting/enchanting/alchemy are skills feeding the same advancement system; enchant/potion bonuses are modifier sources in the stat graph.
equipment_inventory — gear contributes modifier sources (armor, enchantments, set bonuses) into the same aggregation pipeline; carry-weight is a derived stat.
save_load_serialization — must persist base stats + investment sets (never derived ground truth) deterministically; central to respec and migration.
ui_hud — perk constellation UI, level-up flow, skill/stat sheets, respec UI; reads the stat graph and perk DAG.
input_system — bindings for the progression/menu screens and (optionally) hotbar of perk-granted abilities.
modding_runtime — exposes the data schema + stable IDs; depends on the authoring pipeline's ID/versioning scheme.
audio_vfx — level-up / perk-unlock / skill-increase feedback cues (juice that makes progression feel rewarding).
domains.effort_band: L (3-6 mo) for a robust, data-driven, moddable core with tooling on a custom engine; M (1-2 mo) on a mature engine using GAS/ScriptableObjects. Add content authoring of ~18 skills + ~250 perks as a pa...
milestones: M0 (1-2 wk) — Stat graph spine: attribute struct, modifier stack with specified aggregation order (Override>Mult>AddPct>AddFlat), dirty-flag recompute, unit tests proving determinism. One hardcoded skill + one perk prove end-to-end (perk -> modifier -> derived stat changes).

M1 (2-3 wk) — Data-driven definitions: load skills/attributes/curves/perks from schema-validated JSON; XP curve + inverse; level-up event with data reward table. Replace hardcoded content with data. Debug console (setlevel, addperk, addxp).

M2 (3-4 wk) — Skill advancement: SkillUseEvent bus wired to a stub combat/action source; per-action XP weighting + anti-grind falloff; skills feed character level. Per-skill and character XP persist (fixed-point).

M3 (3-4 wk) — Perk DAG + UI: full prereq/rank/exclusion-group evaluator; perk-point economy; first playable perk constellation UI (original visual metaphor) with unlock/preview; perks grant real modifiers and one conditional 'synergy' perk works.

M4 (2-3 wk) — Respec & prestige: investment-set-as-source-of-truth refactor (derived = pure function), perk respec UI + cost gating, skill prestige/legendary reset with refund and economy audit. Save/load round-trips a complex build losslessly.

M5 (3-4 wk) — Authoring tooling: perk-graph node editor + curve editor + live character simulator; bake-to-binary pipeline; CI data validation. Designers author real content without programmer involvement.

M6 (2-3 wk) — Balance & juice: headless balance-sweep harness flags dominant/trap builds across encounter set; tag-predicate linter; level-up/perk/skill feedback cues (sound, VFX, camera). Telemetry hooks for live tuning.

M7 (ongoing) — Modding surface + content: ship/stabilize data schema and stable IDs, save-version migration table, and author the full ~18-skill / ~250-perk content set against the now-frozen pipeline.

domains.summary: The quest system is the spine that converts world state and player action into structured, trackable, rewardable goals. For a Skyrim-class open-world RPG it must support three tiers of content: (1) authored/hand-scripted quests (branching, voiced, story-critical), (2) template-driven "radiant" quests that fill authored shells with runtime-selected actors/locations/items (the genre's signature for near-infinite filler content), and (3) fully emergent/dynamic quests synthesized from simulation eve...
capabilities: Objective & condition model (declarative predicates over world facts)
Alias / casting layer (bind abstract roles to concrete world objects)
Quest-variable store & global flags (cross-quest world state)
Save/load serialization & determinism of quest state
dependencies: persistence_streaming: stable persistent object identity (IDs that survive cell streaming, save/load, and reordering) is a HARD prerequisite for aliasing and save serialization — build this first
event_bus / messaging core: quests are event-driven; need a global, ordered, deterministic event/message system (ON_DEATH, ON_ITEM_ACQUIRED, ON_CELL_ENTER, ON_DIALOGUE_FLAG)
dialogue_system: dialogue both reads quest/global flags (gating lines, branches) and writes them (advancing stages, setting variables); tight bidirectional coupling via the global fact store
navigation_pathfinding: radiant generation needs reachability validation; the journal compass/markers need pathing to the target; alias 'nearest reachable' scoring
ai_behavior / scheduling: quest targets are NPCs whose schedules, factions, and aliveness gate alias fills and objective completion (escort/follow/kill objectives)
inventory_items: 'fetch/deliver N of item' objectives and reward granting read/write inventory
faction_reputation: quest triggers, template selection weights, and conditions depend on faction standing and reputation
economy: reward affordability, bounty/contract boards, and economy-shortage-driven emergent quests
world_state / time: schedules, cooldowns, day/night and calendar gating of quest availability
localization: all journal text, objective text, and radiant flavor-text must route through string tables with slot substitution
ui_hud: journal screen, quest tracker, compass/world markers are the presentation layer over the quest read-model
save_system: shared serialization framework, versioning, and migration infrastructure
domains.effort_band: L (3-6 mo) for a deterministic, save-safe runtime + radiant tier + journal/UI + a basic linter and debugger, for a small team (1-2 systems engineers + 1 tools engineer + design support), ASSUMING the...
milestones: M0 — Deterministic core (first pixel): hardcoded single quest as a data-defined HSM; stages advance via event-bus messages; status enum Running/Completed/Failed; print to console. Proves the runtime loop.

M1 — Objectives & conditions: declarative condition expression-tree over a world-fact interface; objectives show/complete/fail from events; manual-set escape hatch. A 'go here, kill that, return' quest works end-to-end against placeholder world.

M2 — Journal read-model + tracker UI: per-stage log entries (string-table localized), objective checklist, active-objective HUD, and a world marker resolved from the target's live position. Pure projection over quest state.

M3 — Save/load + determinism: full round-trip of stages, objectives, variables, and a seeded serializable RNG; CI fuzz test save->load->save diff is clean; save-versioning + one migration stub in place.

M4 — Alias/casting + broker: alias slots with type/condition filters, reservation table, lazy/late binding, anti-repetition recency, and recovery policy for missing targets on load. Depends on stable persistent IDs.

M5 — Radiant generation: template pool, weighted selection with cooldowns, alias fill via broker, mandatory validation/reachability pass, concurrency caps, and a designer force-generate console. Notice-board pickup UI with original art.

M6 — Tooling & linter: schema-shared quest graph editor (or in-engine debugger via Dear ImGui), static validator catching unreachable stages / dead-end objectives / dangling aliases / missing loc keys, runnable in CI and editor.
M7 (stretch) — Emergent tier: world-tension detection + HTN/GOAP or grammar-based quest synthesis emitting standard QuestDefs into the same pipeline, gated behind a drama manager. Post-launch R&D.
